recipes.name: Brown Sugar and Mustard Ham Glaze
ingredients_raw: 2 tablespoons prepared mustard, or as needed

steps.text: Mix brown sugar and mustard together in a bowl until smooth. If mixture is too thick, stir in more mustard, a little at a time, until the glaze is spreadable. Adjust flavors to your taste, adding more brown sugar for sweetness or more mustard for tang.
Brush glaze over a fully cooked ham during the last 20 to 30 minutes of baking, following the ham’s heating instructions.

raw_recipe.headline: Brown Sugar and Mustard Ham Glaze
raw_recipe.description: This easy brown sugar and mustard ham glaze uses just two ingredients for a sweet and tangy finish that’s perfect for holiday ham.

review.reviewBody: Easy and delicious glaze for ham. I added a bit more mustard as it was too thick and somewhat grainy as you can see in the photo. It cooked down to a nice syrup though and this is definitely a keeper as this used only 2 ingredients and I always have these on hand! Thanks for sharing.

I used an 8 lb Frick's bone-in ham shank portion for this recipe. I added salt & pepper to taste, a little more mustard (spicy dijon deli style), a few dashes of liquid smoke, and a few tsps ground cloves. I wanted just a little sweet yet more smokey tasting ham. I used a basting brush & basted this mixture on my ham. Wrapped it in heavy duty foil. Placed in disposable roasting pan. Some juice did leak out of the foil. But the finishing product tasted succulent. Very moist & flavorful. A great balance of sweet & smokey. Made a beautiful Veteran's Day meal for my Grandpa. He said it was one of the tastiest hams he has ever had. Thank you for this easy, versatile glaze!

Simple and tasty! As suggested in another review, I added a couple dashes of hickory smoke and a tsp of cloves. I used 2 heaping spoonfuls of dijon mustard with the brown sugar and slathered it all over the scored ham and continued to baste as the glaze melted and blended with the ham juices. Once the ham reached temperature I continued the basting under the broiler and it came out beautifully! I added a bit more dijon to the juices to make the gravy because I enjoy the flavour. Turned out excellent!

I only had 1/2 cup brown sugar so I substituted the other 1/2 cup with honey and then used Grey Poupon, cooked it until all sugar was blended and OMG…Incredibly delicious!!!! Thank you for this amazing recipe even though I tweeked it!

This was an easy to prepare glaze for ham, and I did make a variation (as well as using Dijon mustard as other reviewers have suggested). I used a small ham and a larger baking dish, and after glazing, some of the glaze slid to the bottom of the dish and stood a good chance of burning. My Mom suggested adding some orange juice to the baking dish, which I did (enough to cover the bottom) and not only did it prevent burning but it made a delicious sauce for the ham! Next time, the oj is part of the recipe for me.

This glaze was so easy and just as good as the name brand one I usually buy at the deli. I didn't need much glaze, so I just started with a 1/4 cup of brown sugar & added Dijon mustard until it was the right consistency. Perfect. Easy.
This recipe is a keeper! It reminds me of the hams that my Mom used to make when we were kids. And of course, you need the cloves, pineapple rings and cherries too!!

Easy and Love it!!!!! Used Dijon mustard and added 2tsp of pure maple syrup (as another recommended). I had a precooked ham that I warmed for 3 hours with this glaze. It made the ham AWESOME!!!!! Thanks for this easy glaze. It’s a keeper.

Only 4 stars due to alterations. Great recipe for "freshening up" leftover spiral ham. I halved the recipe for just us and add one fresh orange squeezed. I changed the mustard to Dijon. Poured the heated glaze over the slices before microwaving. They were phenomenal!

Very easy to make and my entire family enjoyed it. I smeared this glaze on top of a small ham and baked it in the oven for 40 minutes before broiling it uncovered for an additional 5 minutes. Everyone went back for seconds.

This one worked out well BUT it was a little too dry so I added some pineapple juice and even though I did it still had a nice taste of mustard. I also stuck pineapple chunks on it with toothpicks, and it turned out great the whole family loved it. Great simple glaze recipe.
-Add pineapple juice to desired consistency
-Use pineapple chunks if desired to add to flavor

This is how my mom always made her glaze. Some of my family dont care for glaze, so I usually add a few slices of ham to a separate dish and add the glaze, along with a bit of the juice from the ham, returning to oven to warm.
My fam loved it . I made it to just dip ham in. 👏❤️
It is wonderful as the recipe calls for. Thanks for sharing!
This tasted really good but it takes a lot more mustard than it calls for.
I’ve been doing this glaze for 40 plus years. Everyone loves it. I just adjust the 2 ingredients to make it smooth.
I love the taste and it is easy to prepare.
Needs lots of mustard to make smooth
I added grounded clove to the mixture it gave a little kick
